summary: A complete, disciplined surface with a weak instrument behind it. The panel is the strongest part: 147 named, stable-ID controls across the six sections, 147/147 reachable on a 5x5 elementFromPoint grid and 147/147 operable by real keyboard with a visible focus ring, and the decorative boundary is provably honest - driving Master Level to 0% and toggling Piano ON while a note sounds changes the rendered signal by under 1e-8 RMS. The keybed is exact (73 keys, 43/30, E1-E7, black-key height fraction 0.615) and pointer, independent multi-touch and computer keyboard all reach a clean note lifecycle with correct pitch and blur cleanup. The voice itself is thin: no decay at all (RMS 0.1404 at 0.10 s, 0.1417 at 1.70 s of a held note), a 0.61 Hz beat instead, identical peaks for a top-of-key and bottom-of-key strike, and peak sample 1.528 under 20 notes. Worse, one React defect - a provider default argument re-created on every render in useMidiInput - tears down MIDI on every render, so every MIDI note dies ~0.3 s in and CC64 sustain never holds. With no UI or keyboard sustain either, sustain is unreachable in the shipped build while IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json declares it working.

criteria.label: Piano voice
evidence: Voice is dependable and correctly pitched across the whole keybed: analyser peak bin 257.8 Hz for C4 and 515.6 Hz for C5 (bin width 21.5 Hz), 73 keys E1-E7 all sounding, no dropouts and no console errors in any probe of build/assets/index-QWC0n1_m.js.

No piano decay at all. Holding one key for 2.0 s (real mouse on [data-midi="60"]) gives analyser RMS 0.1404 at t=0.10 s and 0.1417 at t=1.70 s (ratio 1.01) - a flat, organ-like sustain. What varies instead is a 0.61 Hz beat from the declared 4-cent detuned partial: RMS dips to 0.0609 at t=0.85 s and returns to 0.1417 at t=1.70 s, a ~57% amplitude wobble no acoustic piano has.
Release behaves: key-up at t=2.005 s, RMS 0.1229 -> 0.0067 at t=2.304 s -> 0 at t=2.35 s, matching the declared 0.28 s linear release (src/audio/pianoEngine.ts:43).

Dynamics are unreachable from the two inputs a person actually has. Clicking the top of a white key (y=12% of key height) and the bottom (y=92%) both give peak RMS 0.14161 - bit-identical, because Keybed.tsx:26 and useKeyboardInput.ts:39 hard-code velocity 100. Velocity mapping only responds to MIDI (peak RMS 0.00451 at velocity 20 vs 0.17706 at velocity 110).

Clips under load: 20 computer-keyboard notes held together give a peak sample amplitude of 1.528 (full scale is 1.0) and RMS 0.486 at an analyser tapping the node that feeds AudioContext.destination - master gain 0.6 into a DynamicsCompressor (threshold -6, ratio 12) does not keep the sum inside full scale.

criteria.label: Declared source honesty
evidence: The declared source is what actually sounds. IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json declares a generated additive oscillator stack (triangle fundamental + 4-cent detuned sine + octave and twelfth sines) and zero samples; the exercised build matches - it contains only assets/index-QWC0n1_m.js and assets/index-mEt7LStN.css, no audio asset of any kind, and the rendered tone is a static harmonic stack with exactly the 0.61 Hz beat a 4-cent detune at 261.6 Hz predicts (measured wobble period 1.65 s).

The declared routing matches the running graph: instrumenting AudioNode.prototype.connect in the page showed a single AudioContext with one master gain into one DynamicsCompressor into AudioContext.destination, as declared. The UI states it too - the status chip reads "Piano ready (synthesized voice)", and with AudioContext deleted before load it reads "Silent fallback (no audio device)" while still tracking notes (1 voice while a key is held).

One sentence of the same audio.strategy block is contradicted by the build: it claims "sustain (UI/keyboard/MIDI CC64) holds released notes until the damper lifts". There is no UI sustain control and no keyboard sustain mapping anywhere in src (a grep for sustain hits only midi.ts, useMidiInput.ts and three decorative SUSTPED button definitions), and holding Space with focus cleared neither plays nor holds anything - the note was released 0.30 s after key-up with Space still down.

criteria.label: Input coverage
evidence: Pointer works properly: a real mouse press on a white key holds the note for the full 2.0 s press (RMS ~0.14 throughout), sets aria-pressed="true" and class "key white active", shows "1 voice", and releases on mouse-up.

Multi-touch is genuinely independent: two real CDP touch points on [data-midi=60] and [data-midi=67] give "2 voices"; lifting only the second finger leaves "1 voice"; lifting the first leaves "0 voices".

Computer keyboard works: KeyZ down/up gives a full 2.0 s held note with the same envelope as pointer, OS autorepeat is suppressed (e.repeat guard, src/hooks/useKeyboardInput.ts:31), and 20 mapped keys held at once report 20 voices.

Web MIDI is present but unusable in the built app. A MIDI note held for 1500 ms is audible for ~300 ms: RMS 0.1749 at t=0.05 s, 0.0088 at t=0.30 s, 0 from t=0.35 s, with note-off not sent until t=1.50 s, and the voice counter never leaves 0. Cause: src/hooks/useMidiInput.ts:18 defaults `provider = browserMidiProvider()` in the parameter list, so a new function object is created on every render, the effect's [router, provider] dependency changes every render, and its cleanup runs controller.disconnect() + router.releaseOwner('midi') one frame after the note starts. Instrumenting navigator.requestMIDIAccess counted 70 access requests in one short session (2 per MIDI event).

The candidate's own MIDI test passes because it injects a stable midiProvider prop (tests/inputIntegration.test.tsx:24) - exactly the path that does not re-create the provider, so the injectable boundary hides the browser-only defect.

criteria.label: Voice lifecycle
evidence: Sustain is unreachable by any means in the built app. MIDI CC64 down, note on, note off, pedal still down: the tone is gone 0.30 s after note-off (RMS 0.1190 at t=0.20 s, 0.0002 at t=0.45 s, 0 thereafter), because the same per-render MIDI teardown calls handlers.sustain(false) and releases the note. Space does nothing (no mapping), and all three SUSTPED panel buttons are decorative by declaration and measurably inert.

Velocity mapping exists but is only reachable through that broken MIDI path: MIDI velocity 20 -> peak RMS 0.00451, velocity 110 -> 0.17706 (right direction, ~39x); pointer and computer keyboard are fixed at velocity 100 and produce bit-identical peaks (0.14161 for both a top-of-key and a bottom-of-key click).

Deterministic stealing is implemented oldest-first with maxVoices 16 (src/audio/pianoEngine.ts:95,163) and 20 simultaneous keyboard notes play without dropout or error (peak RMS 0.486) - but the status bar reports "20 voices" when at most 16 can be sounding, so the displayed count is the router's held-key count rather than the voice count.
All-notes-off on blur works: with a keyboard note held, dispatching window blur takes the counter 1 -> 0 and the audio from RMS 0.1284 to 0 within 0.35 s.

Disconnect cleanup is incomplete in code: the MIDI statechange handler (src/input/midi.ts:84-90) only calls handlers.sustain(false) and setState('disconnected'); it never releases the notes that device owns - only the hook's unmount cleanup does.

criteria.label: Control feel & decorative boundary
evidence: Every panel control is genuinely operable by pointer. 5x5 document.elementFromPoint grid at 1440x900 with the page unscrolled: 147/147 controls carrying data-control-id resolve to themselves or a descendant on at least one grid point, and 73/73 keys likewise.

Keyboard operation confirmed with real key presses (not synthetic events): 147/147 controls take focus and all 147 change state - 44/44 sliders and 2/2 spinbuttons move on ArrowUp/ArrowDown (Master Level aria-valuetext 70% -> 75%, Home -> 0%), 101/101 buttons act on Enter or Space (aria-pressed false -> true plus class "pressed"; selectors advance their accessible name, e.g. "Piano type: Misc" -> "Piano type: Grand"). Focus is visible: .knob/.fader-track/.drawbar-track/.panel-btn/.wheel-track:focus-visible each get outline 2px solid var(--led-amber).

Pointer drags report state too: dragging Master Level -60 px, Piano layer A level -50 px, drawbar 1 +40 px (aria-valuetext "7 of 8" -> "8 of 8"), mod wheel, synth filter freq, program dial and reverb dry/wet all moved both aria-valuenow and the rendered indicator.

The decorative boundary is honest and measurable: with a note held, driving Master Level to 0% and toggling Piano ON changed the rendered signal by less than 1e-8 RMS (0.125904602924 -> 0.125904603052). No panel control fakes an audio effect, and the status strip says so explicitly: "All panel controls are decorative."

criteria.label: Required Phase 1 controls present
evidence: 147 controls render with stable data-control-id values and non-empty accessible names, none duplicated and none unnamed, split performance 9 / organ 27 / piano 20 / program 22 / synth 36 / effects 33 across the six documented sections in the documented left-to-right order.

Every sectionLandmarks entry is present: nine drawbars with correct footages (16', 5 1/3', 8', 4', 2 2/3', 2', 1 3/5', 1 1/3', 1'), LED ladders, organ model and percussion switches; piano layer levels, type/model selectors, timbre and detail switches; program OLED, large dial, all eight program buttons, page nav, Live Mode, Layer Scene, Store/Split, three morph assigns; synth OLED with osc/filter/env/LFO/arp; effects Mod 1, Mod 2, Amp Sim/EQ, Delay, Comp, Reverb and FX focus; performance Master Level, pitch stick, mod wheel, the Rotary Speaker block and 'nord stage 4' branding. Exactly 2 elements carry .oled and they sit in the program and synth sections, satisfying the only-two-primary-OLEDs gate.

Identifiability is hurt in the Program section: its content overflows the section box by 53.7 px against overflow:hidden, so the primary OLED text is sliced mid-word (renders "A:11 / Nord Sta") and the eighth program button's legend is cut. That follows from the section widths in src/model/controls.ts (0.13 / 0.21 / 0.15 / 0.09 / 0.21 / 0.21) against the spec's 0.14 / 0.20 / 0.085 / 0.125 / 0.25 / 0.20; measured rendered fractions are 0.128 / 0.207 / 0.148 / 0.089 / 0.207 / 0.207, worst deviation 0.063 on piano.

One self-declared naming deviation confirmed on screen: the two modulation blocks are silkscreened "MOD 1"/"MOD 2" where the hardware reads Effect 1 / Effect 2; the control inventory underneath matches.

criteria.label: Required piano feature IDs
evidence: piano.basic-note-lifecycle and piano.basic-status-cleanup are exercised in the running build: note on/off, overlapping notes, one-voice-per-pitch retrigger, blur all-notes-off (1 voice -> 0, audio to zero in 0.35 s), and truthful status in all three states I could force - ready ("Piano ready (synthesized voice)"), fallback with AudioContext removed ("Silent fallback (no audio device)", keys still tracked), and MIDI denied.

piano.basic-inputs is only three-quarters real: pointer, independent multi-touch (2 touches -> 2 voices, lift one -> 1 voice) and the mapped computer keyboard with repeat suppression all work, but MIDI notes are force-released one frame after note-on (audible 0.30 s against a 1.50 s hold).

piano.basic-sustain-polyphony is half-implemented in the shipped build: polyphony and oldest-first stealing are there (20 keys held, 16-voice cap, no dropout, peak RMS 0.486), but no sustain transition is reachable from the UI, the computer keyboard or a MIDI pedal - CC64 held down does not keep a released note sounding (RMS 0.0002 by 0.45 s after note-off).

tests/feature-matrix.json maps all 11 required Phase 1 IDs to non-empty test files, and the gates reproduce on a clean install: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile, then test (71 tests in 9 files), typecheck, lint and build all exit 0, and the fresh build emits the same asset hashes as build/ (index-QWC0n1_m.js, index-mEt7LStN.css).

criteria.label: Declared gaps are accurate
evidence: The large declaration is true: 'every panel control other than the keybed and sustain input is honestly decorative' holds under measurement - 147/147 controls move and report state, and driving them changed the rendered signal by less than 1e-8 RMS. 'No recorded sample sets are bundled in Phase 1' holds too: the published build ships no audio asset, only one JS and one CSS file.

The functional declaration is not true. IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json functional.sustainInput states sustain 'is functional from ... MIDI CC64 and the router API'; in the built app CC64 down + note on + note off leaves silence 0.30 s later (RMS 0.0002 at t=0.45 s) because the MIDI effect tears itself down on every render. functional.keybed likewise claims 'Web MIDI note/velocity ... through one shared note lifecycle', and MIDI notes cannot be held at all (0.30 s of audio against a 1.50 s hold).

audio.strategy additionally claims 'sustain (UI/keyboard/MIDI CC64)'. UI sustain and keyboard sustain do not exist anywhere in the source and are not declared as gaps; the honest note two lines down ('The SUSTPED panel toggles are decorative in Phase 1') contradicts the strategy string rather than qualifying it.

Nothing else undeclared was found missing: the decorative-control inventory, the fallback status path, the injectable audio/MIDI boundaries and the 73-key E1-E7 keybed all match their declarations (73 keys, 43 white, 30 black measured in the DOM; black-key height fraction 0.615 against the declared 0.61).

issues.title: Every MIDI note is force-released one frame after note-on, and CC64 sustain with it
issues.detail: src/hooks/useMidiInput.ts:18 declares `provider: MidiAccessProvider | undefined = browserMidiProvider()` as a default parameter, so a new function identity is produced on every render of App. The effect's dependency array is [router, provider], so the effect tears down and re-subscribes on every render; its cleanup calls controller.disconnect() (which calls handlers.sustain(false)) and router.releaseOwner('midi'). Because a note-on itself re-renders App (activeNotes state), the note it just started is released one frame later. Measured on the published build: a MIDI note held 1500 ms is audible for ~300 ms (RMS 0.1749 at t=0.05 s, 0.0088 at t=0.30 s, 0 from t=0.35 s) and the voice counter never leaves 0; navigator.requestMIDIAccess was called 70 times in one short session. With CC64 held down, a note-off still silences the tone within 0.30 s. The unit test does not catch this because it injects a stable midiProvider prop, which is the one path that does not re-create the provider.

issues.title: Sustain is not reachable by any input in the shipped build
issues.detail: There is no UI sustain control and no computer-keyboard sustain mapping (grep for sustain in src hits only midi.ts, useMidiInput.ts and three decorative SUSTPED button definitions; DEFAULT_KEYBOARD_MAP has no Space entry). Space with focus cleared does nothing - a note released while Space was held decayed normally 0.30 s after key-up. The only wired path, MIDI CC64, is nullified by the per-render MIDI teardown. Phase 1's hard gate lists sustain among the required piano behaviours, and the piano spec requires sustain from UI control, keyboard mapping and CC64.

issues.title: The piano voice has no decay - it is a sustained organ-like tone with a slow beat
issues.detail: A held note stays at constant amplitude: RMS 0.1404 at t=0.10 s and 0.1417 at t=1.70 s of a 2.0 s hold. The only amplitude movement is a 0.61 Hz beat from the 4-cent detuned partial (dip to 0.0609 at t=0.85 s, back to 0.1417 at t=1.70 s, ~57% depth), which reads as a wobble rather than a piano decay. src/audio/pianoEngine.ts schedules attack and release only - no decay segment - and src/audio/webAudioBackend.ts holds the four oscillators at fixed gain for the whole note.

issues.title: No velocity response from pointer or computer keyboard, and clipping under polyphonic load
issues.detail: Keybed.tsx:26 and useKeyboardInput.ts:39 both pass a constant velocity of 100, so a click at 12% of key height and one at 92% produce bit-identical peaks (0.14161); velocity only varies over MIDI (0.00451 at v20 vs 0.17706 at v110), which is itself broken. Separately, 20 keyboard notes held together reach a peak sample amplitude of 1.528 against full scale 1.0 (RMS 0.486) at the node feeding AudioContext.destination, so the master gain 0.6 into DynamicsCompressor(threshold -6, ratio 12) does not prevent hard clipping.

issues.title: The voice counter reports held keys, not sounding voices
issues.detail: The engine caps polyphony at 16 with oldest-first stealing (src/audio/pianoEngine.ts:43,95,163), but the status bar counts NoteRouter's held pitches. Holding 20 mapped keys displays "20 voices" while at most 16 tones can exist. Small, but it is a status line whose whole purpose is truthfulness.

issues.title: Program section clips its own OLED and eighth program button
issues.detail: The program section's content overflows its box by 53.7 px with overflow:hidden, so the primary OLED renders "A:11 / Nord Sta" cut mid-word and the eighth program button's legend is sliced. Root cause is the section-width table in src/model/controls.ts (performance 0.13, organ 0.21, piano 0.15, program 0.09, synth 0.21, effects 0.21) against the spec's 0.14 / 0.20 / 0.085 / 0.125 / 0.25 / 0.20; measured rendered fractions are 0.128 / 0.207 / 0.148 / 0.089 / 0.207 / 0.207, worst deviation 0.063. Every control remains pointer-reachable, so this is legibility rather than loss of inventory.

issues.title: MIDI device disconnect does not release that device's sounding notes
issues.detail: src/input/midi.ts:84-90 handles a port statechange of 'disconnected' by calling handlers.sustain(false) and setState('disconnected') only; it never releases notes the device owns. Nothing in the controller path calls router.releaseOwner('midi') - only the hook's unmount cleanup does. In the shipped build the render-churn defect masks it, but the intended cleanup contract (all-notes-off on disconnect) is not implemented.
